items.author: Zulker Naeen
items.title: Tracing the recruitment trap behind Russia’s war
items.summary: Bangladeshi men paid agents for Russian jobs and ended up on the front lines. Families wait for bodies and answers, and they want the recruiters behind it in a courtroom.

items.author: Walid El Houri
items.title: Egypt’s crackdown on independent media reaches Mada Masr as editor faces trial
items.summary: Egypt has convicted Mada Masr’s editor-in-chief Lina Attalah and ordered the outlet closed, weeks after arresting the whole Matsada2sh newsroom.

items.author: Oiwan Lam
items.title: Unpacking Hong Kong’s rule of law score according to the World Justice Project’s ranking
items.summary: Institutional injustice, such as political nepotism, legal discrimination, and cronyism, is a far worse abusive use of power that creates systematic injustice.

items.author: Nurbek Bekmurzaev
items.title: In Kosovo, a new app makes reporting problems to the government fast and easy
items.summary: Based on the type and location of the problem, the platform is designed to route the report to the appropriate department and allow the citizen to follow what happens afterwards.

items.author: Civic Media Observatory
items.title: The Brazilian left’s quest to ‘tame’ Meta: A narrative of denouncement and resistance
items.summary: In our October edition of Undertones, we examine a movement calling for accountability and coordinated online action to challenge Meta’s problematic content moderation policies and governance practices in Brazil.

items.author: Nurbek Bekmurzaev
items.title: In Kazakhstan, rural women are forming collectives to improve their livelihoods
items.summary: The planned cooperative would support joint advocacy, shared learning, and exploration of funding opportunities for smart-well or shared irrigation infrastructure.

items.author: Guest Contributor
items.title: When chatbots become ‘answer engines’: AI, geopolitics and truth
items.summary: As AI chatbots become everyday sources of information, research from Kosovo raises questions about how these systems present and sometimes distort geopolitical narratives.

items.author: Global Voices Brazil
items.title: How the streets and a social media army led Lula to a historic win in Brazil
items.summary: After ending the first round 2.2 million votes behind his opponent, Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula won the election with a difference of 4 million votes, and will serve a fourth term as president

items.author: Jude Pierre Louis
items.title: How one Haitian entrepreneur found success by supporting all things local
items.summary: Rébetha Charles didn’t initially see herself as an entrepreneur; everything grew out of her core commitment to Haitian farmers by buying their crops, and encouraging consumers to eat local products.

items.author: Daria Dergacheva
items.title: A digital publication sheds light on Turkey’s prison system
items.summary: “For the relatives of people in prison, as well as for national and international human rights organizations and agencies, the information provided by the Prison Agenda publication can be vital.”
